overview: Cooking turns raw fish and animal meat into food that restores Hitpoints. A failed attempt produces a burnt item, which does not heal.
whyItMatters: Bring cooked food when fighting or exploring away from town. Raw and cooked ingredients occupy inventory space, so bank supplies you will not need on your trip.
howToGetStarted: Use raw food on a fire. Shrimp requires level 1, chicken 5, trout 10, boar meat 15, salmon 20, wolf meat 25, tuna 30, and swordfish 40.
connectedSystems: Fishing provides shrimp, trout, salmon, tuna, and swordfish. Chickens, boars, and wolves drop raw meat; Firemaking supplies the temporary fires used to cook it.
nextSteps: Higher-level fish heal more: cooked shrimp restores 3 Hitpoints, trout 5, salmon 7, tuna 9, and swordfish 12. Choose food you can catch and cook, and check its eating delay before combat.

overview: Crafting cuts gems, straps handles, assembles tools and weapons, makes jewelry, and upgrades staffs. Each recipe has its own ingredients, tools, level, and station requirements.
whyItMatters: A forged head or blade is a component. Combine it with the matching strapped handle to make equipment you can use; carrying both parts does not assemble them automatically.
howToGetStarted: Buy basic supplies from the Crafting Teacher in Starter Town. A Chisel cuts gems, while leather straps the handles made through Fletching.
Talk to Elira Gemhand for Moulds of the Trade. Near a crafting bench, use soft clay on her borrowed jewelry, fire each imprinted mould, and return with the ring, amulet, and tiara moulds.
connectedSystems: Mining supplies gems and clay. Smithing makes metal parts and jewelry bases; Fletching makes handles and plain staffs. Tanner Rusk sells leather after Hides of the Frontier.
nextSteps: Use a cut gem with the matching metal jewelry base for gem-set jewelry. For a tool upgrade, check the assembly recipe before making its head and handle so both parts match.

overview: Firemaking uses a Tinderbox to turn logs into temporary fires. The five log types are Logs, Oak Logs, Willow Logs, Maple Logs, and Yew Logs.
whyItMatters: A fire lets you cook food or fire an imprinted clay mould. It lasts 90 ticks, so keep the materials you intend to use nearby.
howToGetStarted: Choose Use on a Tinderbox and select logs in your inventory. Start with Logs at level 1; the recipe table lists the levels for higher wood types.
connectedSystems: Woodcutting supplies logs. General stores stock Tinderboxes, and the resulting fire supports Cooking and mould-making in Crafting.
nextSteps: When a fire burns out, one Ashes item appears on the ground. Take it if you want it, and light another fire if you still have food or moulds to finish.

overview: Fishing catches shrimp, trout, salmon, tuna, and swordfish using a small net, a rod with bait, or a harpoon. The available catches depend on your level and the water.
whyItMatters: Cook your catch for healing food, or sell it to the Fishing Supplier. Keep enough inventory space for catches and enough bait for rod fishing.
howToGetStarted: Buy tools from the Fishing Supplier in Starter Town. Use a Small Net for shrimp at level 1, a Fishing Rod with Bait for trout at 10 and salmon at 20, and a Harpoon for tuna at 30 and swordfish at 40.
connectedSystems: Cooking turns raw fish into food. The Fishing Teacher offers From Net to Harpoon: turn in one each of raw shrimp, trout, salmon, tuna, and swordfish for a Rune Harpoon and 250 Fishing XP.
nextSteps: The Rune Harpoon requires Fishing level 40. After completing the quest, the Fishing Teacher sells a replacement when you carry none. Check the water and method tables below before choosing a fishing spot.

overview: Fletching shapes logs into shafts, handles, unfinished bows, and plain staffs. It also attaches feathers, arrowheads, and bow strings to finish ranged equipment.
whyItMatters: Bows need compatible arrows for combat. Arrow production combines wood from Woodcutting, feathers from suppliers or drops, and arrowheads from Smithing.
howToGetStarted: Use a Knife on logs and choose a recipe. Combine shafts with feathers to make headless arrows, then add matching arrowheads. Combine an unfinished bow with Bow String to finish it.
connectedSystems: Crafting straps wooden handles and uses plain staffs to make elemental staffs. The Fletching Supplier sells supplies; the Advanced Fletcher buys outputs subject to his quest and trade rules.
nextSteps: Check recipe levels for the wood you want to process. Making a bow and equipping it have separate requirements: the recipe uses Fletching, while combat requires the listed Ranged level.

overview: Mining gathers clay, metal ores, coal, uncut gems, and rune essence. Carry a pickaxe and select a rock to begin repeated attempts.
whyItMatters: These materials supply Smithing, Crafting, and Runecrafting. Your level and pickaxe affect access and gathering speed; depleted rocks take time to return.
howToGetStarted: Start with clay, copper, tin, or rune essence at level 1. Copper and tin make bronze bars; iron unlocks at level 10. The node table lists later resources and their requirements.
connectedSystems: Main Overworld has ore, gem, and essence routes. Tutorial Island teaches the copper-and-tin route into Smithing. Crafting cuts uncut gems, while Runecrafting turns essence into runes at altars.
nextSteps: Before a mining trip, check the recipe you are supplying. Higher bars can require coal as well as ore, and jewelry or rune recipes need different materials. Bank extra supplies to free inventory slots.

overview: Runecrafting turns Rune essence into elemental runes at matching altars. Combination runes also require a secondary rune and the combination-crafting unlock.
whyItMatters: Staffs consume compatible runes during magic combat, including missed attacks. Carrying enough runes lets you continue fighting after a trip to the altar.
howToGetStarted: Mine Rune essence with a pickaxe, then use the Ember Altar at level 1. Water unlocks at 10, Earth at 20, Air at 30, and combination recipes at 40.
connectedSystems: Mining supplies essence. The Rune Tutor and Combination Sage sell runes and related supplies in Starter Town; their trade and unlock rules are listed below.
nextSteps: Small, Medium, and Large pouches hold extra essence subject to their level and capacity rules. For a combination recipe, check both the altar and secondary rune before travelling.

overview: Smithing smelts ore into bars at a furnace and forges metal parts, armor, and arrowheads at an anvil. Furnace recipes also make silver and gold jewelry bases.
whyItMatters: Forged armor can be equipped directly, but tool heads and sword blades need Crafting assembly with a matching strapped handle. Arrowheads need Fletching assembly before they become arrows.
howToGetStarted: Mine copper and tin, then use a furnace to make Bronze Bars. Take bars and a Hammer to an anvil and choose a forging recipe. Starter Town has both stations.
connectedSystems: Mining provides ore and coal. Crafting assembles tools, weapons, and gem-set jewelry; Fletching uses arrowheads. Borin Ironvein and Thrain Deepforge support the metal trade in Main Overworld.
nextSteps: Plan the number of bars before smelting. Each armor piece, head, or blade has its own level and material cost; the recipe table lists them along with XP and required tools.

overview: Woodcutting gathers Logs, Oak Logs, Willow Logs, Maple Logs, and Yew Logs with an axe. Select a tree to begin repeated chopping attempts.
whyItMatters: Logs can become fires, bows, arrows, handles, or staffs. Higher wood types have their own level requirements and produce different equipment through Fletching.
howToGetStarted: Carry an axe and start with Normal Trees. Oak unlocks at level 10, Willow at 20, Maple at 30, and Yew at 40. The node table lists XP, difficulty, and respawn timing.
connectedSystems: Firemaking burns logs with a Tinderbox. Fletching shapes them with a Knife, and Crafting straps the resulting handles for tool and weapon assembly.
nextSteps: Choose the wood type needed by your next recipe. You can use an axe for Woodcutting while carrying it; equipping it as a weapon has a separate Attack requirement.
